title: Admin VPC + HSM journeys and error states
content:
Purpose and scope:
Notes focused on admin console UX for private deployments: the journeys when linking a customer VPC, importing/attaching KMS keys, and HSM onboarding. Goal is to capture common failure modes, recovery paths, and concise copy that reduces operator mistake rates. This is intentionally rough — wireframe-level plus backlog items.

Personas in focus:
- Infra owner (primary): cloud/network engineer, knows VPCs, routing, IAM, but unfamiliar with Redwood primitives.
- Platform admin: product/SRE who will run Dedicated in a customer VPC, cares about auditability and minimal blast radius.
- Solutions engineer: may assist on first deploy and expects clear diagnostics and reproducible steps.

High-level journeys (happy path)
1) Create private deployment record -> choose region -> pick deployment type (VPC peering / Shared VPC / PrivateLink) -> enter VPC id & subnets -> validate connectivity -> attach KMS key or choose HSM -> finalize and schedule provisioning.
2) KMS flow: select KMS provider (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure KeyVault) -> guided IAM role creation (one-click role template + CLI snippet) -> verify grant -> import key metadata -> optionally rotate test key -> confirm.
3) HSM flow (for HSM-enabled plans): request HSM allocation -> present cost/latency note -> provide operator checklist for network egress rules and NTP, HA endpoints -> confirm and create cluster.

Wireframe notes (console panels)
- Top-level: "Deployment summary" card with region, VPC id, status badge (Pending/Healthy/Degraded/Failed). Small inline link: "Open connectivity test".
- VPC panel: show subnet table with route table summaries (CIDR, AZ, route targets). For each subnet show a quick health indicator derived from our probe and customer route table presence. If missing, show exact missing route suggestion with one-click copy-to-clipboard CLI.
- Keys/HSM panel: 3-column layout: Key status | Owner/ARN | Last verified. If key not found or permission error, show minimal wording and a single-step remediation called "Grant Redwood access" that expands to curated CLI + IAM JSON and a one-click GitHub gist download.
- Activity / logs: streaming trace lines from our connectivity checker (tcp handshake, TLS negotiation) and redacted from PII. Allow copy of full trace for ticket creation.

Common error states and UX handling (priority order)
A) VPC validation: missing route to our egress (peering/VPN)
  - Symptom: validation fails with "No route to 10.2.0.0/16"
  - Why it happens: customer forgot to add route to peering attachment, or route table bound to wrong subnet.
  - Console behavior: show clear cause + explicit remediation steps. Offer two remediation actions: "Show CLI snippet" and "Send suggested change to owner" (pre-populated email/SN).
  - Copy suggestion: "Your VPC does not route traffic to Redwood's peering attachment. Add a route to <REDWOOD_PEER_PREFIX> via the peering attachment. Need help? Click 'Contact solutions'."
  - Telemetry: attach validation_id to logs and surface in UI so support can reference INF-4120 style tickets.

B) KMS permission denied (AccessDenied)
  - Symptom: API calls return 403 when verifying key usage/DescribeKey.
  - Console behavior: show exact permission missing like kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey. Provide least-privilege role JSON that contains only required actions and a prescriptive role name.
  - UX: allow operator to copy a single policy blob, and a toggle to reveal an expanded explanation for security reviewers.
  - Copy suggestion: "Redwood cannot access the key. Grant the following permissions to the Redwood service principal: kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:DescribeKey. Example policy attached."

C) HSM: cluster initialization timed out
  - Symptom: HSM nodes fail to join, provisioning stuck > 30m.
  - Why: NTP drift, firewall blocking management port, wrong subnet with no NAT for updates.
  - Console: show timeline with last successful step and a single 'Retry init' button that will re-run post-install validation. Also surface a 'Run local agent check' with a small downloadable script that customers can run and paste output into UI.
  - Copy suggestion: "Initialization did not complete. Check that HSM nodes can reach our update endpoints and that system time is accurate. If you want Redwood engineers to debug, click 'Share debug bundle' to upload logs."

D) Region mismatch (model image unavailable in chosen region)
  - Symptom: Provisioning fails due to image not found or insufficient capacity.
  - Console behavior: detect fallback-compatible variants and propose alternate regions or smaller instance types. Show cost/latency delta.
  - Copy suggestion: "Selected region does not currently have the model image. We can deploy in <alt-region> with expected +X ms latency and ~Y% cost change. Accept suggestion or choose a different model."

Design patterns for error recovery (UI primitives)
- Single source of truth for remediation: every validation error emits: (a) human-readable reason, (b) machine-readable error code, (c) one-click remediation items (copy CLI, prefill support ticket, toggle advanced).
- Minimal cognitive load: avoid showing full IAM JSON by default. Use collapsible "advanced" sections.
- Repro scripts: generate a small sanitized diagnostic bundle with an id that can be attached to tickets — this id maps to stored logs and retry caches.
- Confirm-before-destructive: when operator rotates keys, warn about active sessions and suggest rolling window steps with automated grace period.

Backlog (rough grooming)
- PD-001: "Validation UI: show missing route details + apply template" (priority: high, estimate: 3).
- PD-002: "KMS least-privilege role templates + one-click copy" (priority: high, estimate: 2).
- PD-003: "HSM init retry and debug bundle flow" (priority: high, estimate: 5).
- PD-004: "Region-fallback recommender with cost/latency estimates" (priority: medium, estimate: 3).
- PD-005: "Connectivity trace streaming component" (priority: medium, spike: 2).
- PD-006: "Support ticket prefill + attach diagnostic id" (priority: low, estimate: 1).

Acceptance criteria (first three items)
- PD-001: console shows route table mismatches with suggested route rules; copyable CLI snippet present; automated validation passes after user updates route.
- PD-002: KMS flow returns machine-readable permission list; admin can copy role/policy; test verification succeeds when policy attached.
- PD-003: Retry button re-runs init, logs are captured and linked to ticket id; debug bundle includes probe outputs.

Edge cases and unresolved questions
- Should we allow Redwood to create IAM roles automatically in customer accounts? Pros: reduces errors. Cons: trust/sales/security friction. Proposal: provide a 'propose role' feature that generates a CloudFormation/Terraform template rather than creating roles directly.
- HSM licensing/per-instance fees need explicit warning in UI. Where to show: prior to HSM request, show a modal with cost and SLA impact.
- Offline customers (air-gapped): need a different flow — provide downloadable agent + manual log upload flow. Add PD-007 for air-gap later.
- Error language localization: currently English-only; flag for future.

Copy quick bank (short messages)
- Success badge: "Connected — agent verified"
- Warning: "Partial connectivity — missing routes to peering"
- Error: "Unable to verify key permissions (403) — see required permissions"
- HSM init: "Initializing (this may take up to 45 minutes)"
- Fallback suggestion: "Deploy to alt-region (recommended)"

Notes to self / next steps:
- Sync with SRE about adding explicit validation IDs in logs (CC: @Ethan).
- Ask legal for minimal policy language approval before shipping role templates (JIRA INF-4238).
- Prepare a short demos script for solutions eng using the new debug bundle (target: internal demo 2025-09-10).

Appendix: small CLI snippets to surface in the console (examples, redact before shipping)
- Route add (aws): aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0123 --destination-cidr-block 10.135.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-abc123
- KMS role sample (AWS managed policy): {
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
    "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:...:key/..."
  }]
}

This doc is a working draft — please add comments inline or ping in #private-deploy with suggested copy or flows.
